newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Pinochet backpedals on coup suggestion.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Pinochet backpedals on coup suggestion.

text.p: Former military ruler Gen. Augusto Pinochet sought to play down on Wednesday his suggestion that Chile's armed forces might stage another coup like the one in 1973 that overthrew a socialist government.
Pinochet, 80, denied his remark was aimed at a popular socialist cabinet minister expected to run for president in 1999 and said he would probably be dead by then anyway.
"What do you want? Even if it happened that way, the most likely thing is I won't be in this world by then," he told reporters.

Pinochet implied on Tuesday the military might someday carry out a coup similar to that which overthrew Marxist president Salvador Allende in September 1973 and brought them to power for nearly 17 years.

"We arrived in the year 1973, when a socialist president had left. And take care -- we could do it again," Pinochet said in a jocular tone in a speech to rightist supporters in a Santiago social club.

Local news media took the statement to be a reference to Public Works Minister Ricardo Lagos, a socialist and opponent of Pinochet during military rule who holds a wide lead in public opinion polls for the 1999 elections.
But Pinochet quashed that idea, saying: "I was never talking about Lagos, and anyway, I'll be dead by then."
Lagos, who has been building bridges to the military and recently appeared in public with Pinochet, and other government officials moved swiftly to minimise the importance of Pinochet's remarks.
"I get the impression he was saying it in jest," Lagos told reporters. "He was speaking in a joking tone."

Pinochet handed over to an elected civilian president in March 1990 after nearly 17 years in power but remains army commander-in-chief and is the undisputed ideological leader of Chile's powerful armed forces.
